result.markdown: --- title: "Visualizing Soccer Data" description: "Exploring Argentina vs. Saudi Arabia match via Data viz using Python " date: "2026-05-25" categories: [Python, EDA, Soccer, Data, Visualization, StatsBomb] format: html: code-fold: true code-tools: true jupyter: python3 --- ## Overview I had used R, ggplot2, ggsoccer and other R packages to build visualizations for my 2022 world cup microsite showcasing Argentina's progress In this blog post, I'm using Python to explore building a few different set of visualizations for the Argentina vs. Saudi Arabia game ## Tools Used - **Languages:** Python - **IDE:** Positron - **Packages:** quarto, pandas, numpy, mplsoccer ## Python Imports ::: {#84f55314 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import matplotlib.patches as mpatches from mplsoccer import Pitch, VerticalPitch, Sbopen import pandas as pd import numpy as np ``` ::: ## Finding the match id's for Argentina's games ::: {#afdcd220 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # https://mplsoccer.readthedocs.io/en/latest/gallery/statsbomb/plot_statsbomb_data.html#match-data parser = Sbopen() # 2022 World Cup matches = parser.match(competition_id=43, season_id=106) TEAM = "Argentina" team_matches = matches[ (matches['home_team_name'] == TEAM) | (matches['away_team_name'] == TEAM) ] print(team_matches[['match_id', 'home_team_name', 'away_team_name', 'match_date']].to_string()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` match_id home_team_name away_team_name match_date 24 3869321 Netherlands Argentina 2022-12-09 27 3869685 Argentina France 2022-12-18 30 3869151 Argentina Australia 2022-12-03 38 3857264 Poland Argentina 2022-11-30 39 3857289 Argentina Mexico 2022-11-26 42 3869519 Argentina Croatia 2022-12-13 56 3857300 Argentina Saudi Arabia 2022-11-22 ``` ::: ::: Match id 3857300 is for the specific game: Argentina vs Saudi Arabia ## Loading the dataframes ::: {#07527dbf .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Load match events # https://mplsoccer.readthedocs.io/en/latest/gallery/statsbomb/plot_statsbomb_data.html#event-data events, related, freeze, tactics = parser.event(3857300) # Argentina passes arg_passes = events[ (events['type_name'] == 'Pass') & (events['team_name'] == 'Argentina') ] # Saudi Arabia passes ksa_passes = events[ (events['type_name'] == 'Pass') & (events['team_name'] == 'Saudi Arabia') ] # Argentina shots arg_shots = events[ (events['type_name'] == 'Shot') & (events['sub_type_name'] !='Penalty') & (events['team_name'] == 'Argentina') ] # Saudi Arabia shots ksa_shots = events[ (events['type_name'] == 'Shot') & (events['sub_type_name'] !='Penalty') & (events['team_name'] == 'Saudi Arabia') ] print(f"Argentina passes: {len(arg_passes)}, shots: {len(arg_shots)}") print(f"Saudi Arabia passes: {len(ksa_passes)}, shots: {len(ksa_shots)}") print("* excluding penalties") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Argentina passes: 646, shots: 14 Saudi Arabia passes: 286, shots: 3 * excluding penalties ``` ::: ::: ## Function setup ::: {#9a42343f .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} def get_pre_shot_passes(passes_df, shots_df): """Get passes made within 15 seconds of a shot""" pre_shot = [] # empty list to collect results for _, shot in shots_df.iterrows(): #looping through every shot one at a time shot_time = shot['minute'] * 60 + shot['second'] # converting shot time to total seconds window = passes_df[ (passes_df['minute'] * 60 + passes_df['second']) .between(shot_time - 15, shot_time) #convert every pass time to total seconds # then find passes that happened within the 15 second window BEFORE the shot ] pre_shot.append(window) # add to results list return pd.concat(pre_shot).drop_duplicates() if pre_shot else pd.DataFrame() # combine all results # remove duplicates # return empty dataframe if nothing is found arg_pre_shot = get_pre_shot_passes(arg_passes, arg_shots) ksa_pre_shot = get_pre_shot_passes(ksa_passes, ksa_shots) ``` ::: ## 1. Pass Map Viz - Buildup to the Shot ::: {#be841a4e .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(16, 8)) fig.patch.set_facecolor('#ffffff') fig.suptitle('Pass Buildup to Shot (Within 15 Seconds)', color='black', fontsize=14, y=1.02) for ax, passes_df, team, color in zip( axes, [arg_pre_shot, ksa_pre_shot], ["Argentina", "Saudi Arabia"], ['#75AADB', '#00b100'] ): pitch = Pitch( pitch_type='statsbomb', pitch_color='#fafafa', line_color='#cccccc', line_zorder=2 ) pitch.draw(ax=ax) # complete passes complete = passes_df[passes_df['outcome_name'].isna()] if not complete.empty: pitch.arrows( complete.x, complete.y, complete.end_x, complete.end_y, ax=ax, color=color, width=2, headwidth=4, alpha=0.8, label='Complete' ) # incomplete passes incomplete = passes_df[passes_df['outcome_name'].notna()] if not incomplete.empty: pitch.arrows( incomplete.x, incomplete.y, incomplete.end_x, incomplete.end_y, ax=ax, color='#333333', width=1.5, headwidth=3, alpha=0.5, label='Incomplete' ) ax.set_title(team, color='black', fontsize=13, pad=10) ax.legend(facecolor='#fafafa', labelcolor='#333333', loc='upper left', fontsize=8) plt.tight_layout() plt.savefig('images/pass_map.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='#fafafa') plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/cell-6-output-1.png){width=482 height=788} ::: ::: 🟦 Argentina Takeaways 1. The high volume of passes show that Argentina dominated possession 2. Short and quick arrows are clustered together meaning a lot of tight passing was carried out 3. Argentina controlled the ball and recycled possession heavily in the opponent's half creating a sustained attacking pressure 🟩 Saudi Takeways 1. Saudi Arabia sat deeper, played fewer passes and relied on direct balls when they played forward
